tier_justification: The correspondence between universally conjunctive predicate transformers and relations (demonic updates) is textbook material and is mechanized in Isabelle/HOL (Struth 2018); restated here with the inverse map relOf exposed.
plain_claim: For any state type, a predicate transformer T distributes over the conjunction of every family of postconditions - including the empty family and infinite families - if and only if T = wlp (relOf T), where relOf T s s' holds iff s' satisfies every postcondition that T establishes from s; and relOf (wlp R) = R, so the representing relation is unique.

nonvacuity_witness: ConjAll (wlp stepR) holds for the two-way choice on Nat and ConjAll eventually fails, so both sides of the equivalence occur; relOf_wlp_skipR is a concrete instance of the inverse equation.
non_claims: Does not say binary or finite conjunctivity suffices; it does not (see finitary-laws-not-relational).
Says nothing about termination: wlp R holds at a state without R-successors for every postcondition, and a universally conjunctive transformer need not be strict.

Two readings are covered and must not be conflated: wlp R as the partial-correctness weakest liberal precondition (a state without successors models guaranteed divergence) and wlp R as the total-correctness demonic update [R] = wp R True of a never-aborting program (a state without successors is a miracle). A paired (wp, wlp) semantics of a possibly aborting program is not modeled; in such a semantics wlp is not determined by wp.
Does not imply binary disjunctivity: wlp R distributes over disjunction only when every state has at most one R-successor; for the nondeterministic two-way choice it fails (not_disjBin_wlp_stepR).
relOf T is an arbitrary relation; nothing says it is computable, total, finitely branching, or denoted by a program of any particular language.
Equality is extensional equality of functions on predicates; nothing is claimed about syntactic or intensional identity.
One state type only; relations between different input and output state types are not formalized.

tier_justification: Both directions are classical: continuity of wp for boundedly nondeterministic mechanisms and its failure for unbounded choice (Dijkstra 1976, ch. 9; the title of EWD 675 states the equivalence; Plotkin 1980 and Wand 1977 in the strict setting on a countable state set). Restated here for an arbitrary pair (R, term) over an arbitrary state type; that no countability of the state type is needed follows from the fact that an infinite set has a countably infinite subset (using choice).
plain_claim: For any state type, wp R term is omega-continuous (establishing the union of an increasing Nat-indexed chain of postconditions implies establishing one member) if and only if every start state in term has a finite R-image, i.e. all its successors lie in one list. No countability or other hypothesis on the state type is needed.

hypotheses.name: chains rather than arbitrary countable families in OmegaContinuous

hypotheses.purpose: needed: the backward direction, restricted to the one-point state type, implies the limited principle of omniscience by a proof that uses no axiom, so it is not constructively provable. Reason: FiniteImage gives a list containing every successor without deciding which list members are successors. Lean's logic is classical, so no countermodel can be exhibited inside Lean; this reverse implication is the witness.

hypotheses.name: axiom of choice (forward direction: omega-continuity implies finite image)
hypotheses.purpose: used to extract an injective sequence from an image contained in no list; whether the forward direction needs choice (or excluded middle) was not determined

nonvacuity_witness: The two-way choice on Nat is omega-continuous with finite images and havoc on Nat is neither; with the partial non-abortion predicate 'nonzero', zeroHavocR satisfies both sides and havoc fails both.
non_claims: Finite does not mean uniformly bounded: image sizes may grow without bound across states.

FiniteImage bounds the set of final states of the input/output relation, not the branching of an operational transition system: infinitely many execution paths with finitely many final states still give an omega-continuous wp; no operational semantics (and no Konig's lemma) is formalized.
Miracles are omega-continuous: a state in term with an empty R-image has a finite image (omegaContinuous_wp_emptyR). Omega-continuity implies neither strictness nor feasibility.
Nothing is constrained about R outside term: an omega-continuous wp R term may have infinite images at aborting states (omegaContinuous_wp_partial_infinite_image_outside_term).

OmegaContinuous is the one-sided upward (or-) continuity law for increasing chains. On its own it admits non-monotone transformers such as pointwise negation (omegaContinuous_negT_not_monotone); for monotone transformers, such as every wp, it coincides with the two-sided equation (omegaContinuous_two_sided_iff). Downward (and-) continuity over decreasing chains already holds for every wp, as a case of positive conjunctivity.
Omega-continuity is not necessary for being a wp: havoc on Nat is universally conjunctive and strict but not omega-continuous (havocR_nat_conjAll_strict_not_omegaContinuous).
Omega-continuity alone does not make a transformer relational: angelic choice is omega-continuous and not a wp.
Nothing is proved about loops, recursion or fixed points; the role of continuity in computing the wp of a loop is not formalized.
Only Nat-indexed chains are used here; continuity over directed families is defined (DirContinuous) and used only in directed-continuity-forces-conjunctivity.

non_claims: The example is not omega-continuous, so it does not show that Dijkstra's list (strict, monotone, binary conjunctive, continuous) fails to characterize wp; on state types that inject into Nat -> Bool that list does characterize the boundedly nondeterministic, miracle-free wp's (strict_conjBin_omegaContinuous_iff_wp_finiteImage_totalOn_of_continuumState), and with continuity over directed families the binary law suffices on every state type.

Whether a binary conjunctive, omega-continuous transformer that is not a wp exists on some state type that does not inject into Nat -> Bool is left open. (Informal remark, not formalized and not checked against a source: such an example would yield a countably complete non-principal ultrafilter, so it cannot be constructed without large-cardinal assumptions.)

Does not show that adding binary disjunctivity (T (P or Q) = T P or T Q, Dijkstra's law for deterministic mechanisms) would make the finitary laws sufficient: eventually is not binary disjunctive (not_disjBin_eventually), so this example says nothing about that longer list. (Informal remark, not formalized: membership in a non-principal ultrafilter on Nat satisfies all those laws and is not relational.)
No general statement about 'every finitary law' is made; exactly the listed laws (and conjunctivity over finite lists) are shown insufficient.

The example is not meaningless: it is an angelic choice of a threshold followed by a demonic choice (eventually_eq_angelicDemonic, eventually_iff_exists_fromN). It lies outside relational semantics only.
Nothing is claimed about any particular verification framework; whether a framework's own transformer type admits an analogous inhabitant must be checked against its definitions.

design_question: Which laws must a verification framework demand of a weakest-precondition transformer so that every admitted transformer is the wp of some relational (possibly nondeterministic, possibly aborting) program, without excluding honest programs? tier_justification: The criterion is mechanized in Isabelle/HOL (Preoteasa 2014, lemma assert_demonic_refinement) and, with return values, in Coq (Alpuim and Swierstra 2018, Theorem soundness); the chaos-normal-form corollary is spelled out here.
plain_claim: wp R1 t1 is refined by wp R2 t2 (every guarantee of the first is a guarantee of the second) if and only if t1 is included in t2 and, on start states in t1, every R2-outcome is an R1-outcome; no normal form is assumed. If moreover (R1, t1) is in chaos normal form, the second condition may be replaced by the global inclusion of R2 in R1.

hypotheses.name: (refinedBy_wp_iff) relation inclusion is restricted to non-aborting start states of the refined program
hypotheses.purpose: outside t1 the first program guarantees nothing, so nothing constrains R2 there: abort, presented with the empty relation, is refined by havoc although havoc's relation is not included in the empty one

hypotheses.name: (both statements) inclusion of non-abortion predicates
hypotheses.purpose: relation inclusion alone does not give refinement, even for pairs in chaos normal form

hypotheses.name: (refinedBy_wp_iff_of_chaosNormal) ChaosNormal R1 t1
hypotheses.purpose: without it the global form fails: the witness is not in chaos normal form, refinement holds, and the global criterion fails

hypotheses.name: (refinedBy_wp_iff) classical logic
hypotheses.purpose: not needed: refinedBy_wp_iff is proved using no axiom at all: audit/axioms.json records an empty axiom list for it

hypotheses.name: (refinedBy_wp_iff_of_chaosNormal) classical logic
hypotheses.purpose: needed: the global form, restricted to the one-point state type, implies excluded middle by a proof that uses no axiom. Lean's logic is classical, so no countermodel can be exhibited inside Lean; this reverse implication is the witness.

nonvacuity_witness: havoc on Nat is refined by the two-way choice and not conversely; with the partial non-abortion predicate 'nonzero', the partial decrement is refined by the total-domain decrement and not conversely; the chaos normal form of the partial decrement satisfies all hypotheses and both sides of the global form.
non_claims: Refinement here is pointwise implication of wp (the total-correctness refinement order of the refinement calculus); it is not Nelson's approximation order defined from wp and wlp jointly, not an Egli-Milner order, and not trace refinement, simulation, or data refinement.
A refinement may delete all outcomes: a miracle refines everything, so 'refines' does not imply 'implementable'.

The relational criterion applies to wp-transformers only. For arbitrary transformers, inclusion of termOf and reverse inclusion of relOf on termOf do not imply refinement: magic (the demonic update of the empty relation) and eventually have the same termOf and relOf, yet magic is not refined by eventually (relational_criterion_fails_off_wp).
The global inclusion form needs the refined pair in chaos normal form (refinedBy_wp_global_inclusion_needs_chaosNormal), and classical logic; the restricted form needs neither.

tier_justification: The angelic-update/demonic-update normal form of monotonic predicate transformers and the correspondence with up-closed multirelations are textbook material.
plain_claim: A predicate transformer is monotone if and only if it is an angelic choice of demonic updates, T Q s iff there is a set P available at s all of whose members satisfy Q, where one may take 'P is available at s' to mean T P s (the multirelation multirelOf T); and multirelOf recovers a multirelation A from its transformer angelicDemonic A if and only if A is up-closed, giving a one-to-one correspondence between monotone transformers and up-closed multirelations. Non-up-closed multirelations can induce the same transformer as an up-closed one.

hypotheses.name: monotonicity (first statement)
hypotheses.purpose: every transformer of the angelic/demonic form is monotone; negation is not monotone and is not of that form

hypotheses.name: up-closure (second statement)
hypotheses.purpose: multirelOf returns an up-closed multirelation, so a multirelation that is not up-closed is not recovered from its transformer

nonvacuity_witness: eventually is monotone and equal to the transformer of its multirelation, negation is neither; 'all sets containing the current state' is up-closed and recovered, the singleton multirelation is neither; eventually and every wp are exhibited with explicit multirelations.
non_claims: Near-definitional: the multirelation of T is T itself with its arguments swapped; the statement carries no information beyond monotonicity.
Uniqueness holds only among up-closed multirelations: an up-closed multirelation and a non-up-closed one can induce the same transformer (upClosed_not_unique_among_all, angelicDemonic_not_injective).
Does not say monotone transformers have relational semantics: angelic choice and eventually do not.
No game semantics is formalized; 'angel' and 'demon' are readings of the existential and universal quantifiers.

plain_claim: On a state type that injects into Nat -> Bool - in particular on every countable state type, and on the uncountable type Nat -> Bool itself - every predicate transformer that is binary conjunctive and omega-continuous is conjunctive over all nonempty families. Strictness and top preservation are not assumed.

hypotheses.name: ContinuumState (the state type injects into Nat -> Bool)
hypotheses.purpose: lets the state type be coded by bit sequences, so that omega-continuity bounds the splitting of the tree of 'positive' prefixes. Necessity is unknown: it is not necessary for countable state types or for Nat -> Bool (both satisfy it), and no counterexample on a larger state type is given. (Informal remark, not formalized and not checked against a source: a counterexample would yield a countably complete non-principal ultrafilter, so it cannot be constructed without large-cardinal assumptions.) With continuity over directed families no hypothesis on the state type is needed (directed-continuity-forces-conjunctivity).

hypotheses.name: ConjBin
hypotheses.purpose: monotonicity plus omega-continuity is not enough

hypotheses.name: OmegaContinuous
hypotheses.purpose: binary conjunctivity alone is not enough on an infinite state type

hypotheses.name: classical logic
hypotheses.purpose: needed: the statement (and already its countable special case), restricted to the one-point state type, implies excluded middle by a proof that uses no axiom. Lean's logic is classical, so no countermodel can be exhibited inside Lean; this reverse implication is the witness.

nonvacuity_witness: Nat -> Bool injects into itself, is not countable, and the wp of skip on it is binary conjunctive and omega-continuous; Nat is countable and the wlp of the two-way choice is binary conjunctive and omega-continuous.
non_claims: ContinuumState is a sufficient hypothesis whose necessity is unknown (not proved tight). State types that do not inject into Nat -> Bool, such as (Nat -> Bool) -> Bool, are outside this theorem's hypotheses; no counterexample on them is claimed.

Uncountable state types are not excluded: Nat -> Bool is covered (nat_to_bool_uncountable_conjBin_omegaContinuous_conjNonempty), so countability is not necessary. The countable special case conjNonempty_of_conjBin_of_omegaContinuous_of_countable is kept as a corollary for alignment with Wand 1977 and Plotkin 1980; its hypothesis CountableState is known to be stronger than necessary.
OmegaContinuous is the one-sided law of the definitions; here ConjBin implies monotonicity, so it coincides with two-sided omega-continuity.
The conclusion is conjunctivity over nonempty families, not over all families.

Via the wp and continuity characterizations the representing program is boundedly nondeterministic on its non-aborting states (conjBin_omegaContinuous_iff_wp_finiteImage_of_continuumState), so this route never yields unbounded nondeterminism.
